items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: So Bernie got these fellas together and we formed a little band.

ctx.x: So when was the first music that you were interested in? Did you start on the trombone or which instrument did you start on?

Well, my first instrument was trombone, but it wasn't my favorite instrument. I'd like to tell you, Bill, about how I come to study the trombone. While talking with Joe Oliver, it must have been somewhere around 1920, 1921, somewhere along there. He, I told Joe Oliver that I was going to take lessons on the trombone. So he says, why don't you try the clarinet? The reason Joe suggested to me to take the, take up the clarinet was because I used to whistle so good. And he said people did. So he thought if a fella…

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Yeah, not with Art Sims, because Art Sims died. But between the two leaders, Arthur Albright and Bernie Sims.

ctx.x: I think Audis Starks was on there, Clamondon and Saxe.

So we came back, Pay Night and Padlock was on the place. I know 5250 was paying us. I didn't really get that money, I just said married to. And so then I went and joined Arthur Sims in Milwaukee at the Wisconsin Roof. And so after about a year with Arthur, Arthur caught pneumonia in August and died. So then a fellow who is now a physician, Arthur Albright, he was the oldest man in the band. He was a guitar player and banjoist. So he was taking over the band and then he left to go to Meharry to study medicine.…
